_doc: LIVE-MCP scenario registry. Derived from marketplace_test_bank.json's journey lane by tools/build_live_mcp_registry.py - do not hand-edit the rows, edit the CATEGORIES table and regenerate. `status` moves owed -> walked -> green as the flywheel turns; findings accumulate per scenario so a re-walk can prove a fix rather than re-discover it.

categories.A-discovery: can a stranger FIND the thing they came for? (40% of simulated journey failures died here)
categories.B-listing-lifecycle: can a seller get a listing from nothing to live, and know why when they cannot?
categories.C-inquiry: can a buyer reach a human, and does the seller learn about it?
categories.D-service-hail: can a client raise a job and a provider take it, both knowing what state it is in?
categories.E-money: at the moment money moves, does every screen agree on the number?
categories.F-credits: does a person understand what credits are, what they hold, and what they will get back?
categories.G-trust: is a trust signal earned, visible, and impossible to mint for yourself?
categories.H-moderation: can an admin act, and is a non-admin visibly refused rather than silently ignored?
categories.I-map: does the map tell the truth about where someone is, and stay quiet when it should not?
categories.J-degraded: offline, slow, or failing: does the product REFUSE OUT LOUD instead of pretending?
categories.K-a11y: keyboard, screen reader, contrast, focus order - can this be used without a mouse or good eyes?
categories.L-comprehension: is the wording readable, translated, and free of jargon at the moment it costs money?
categories.M-mobile: at 390 CSS pixels, is every control reachable and every target big enough?
categories.N-continuity: does the page hold its shape while data arrives, and survive a reload mid-flow?
categories.O-empty-error: does an empty state promise only what the product can deliver?
categories.Q-payment-rails: THREE GCash accounts meet here - the buyer's, the provider's, and the founder's personal 0995 009 2416 - and only one of them may ever be on a given screen. WorkHive has no business registration and therefore no merchant account, so every rail is a personal number: a buyer pays the PROVIDER directly and the platform never touches it, while a provider tops up credits by paying the FOUNDER. Put the founder's number on a buyer's payment step and the buyer sends job money to someone who is not party to the job, cannot fulfil it, and cannot reconcile it - and nothing errors. This is also the friction Ian named by hand: 'hassle free ... like the hassle of payment two gcash accounts'. A buyer must see exactly ONE number.
categories.P-isolation: can one tenant see or touch another's rows, through any screen?
categories.S-adversarial: when a guard refuses someone, does the SCREEN teach them why - or just go quiet? The 500 simulations proved the economics hold; none of them looked at a page
categories.T-two-context: buyer and provider signed in AT THE SAME TIME, acting on one job. Every walk so far has been one identity at a time, so races, stale views and 'who sees the state change first' are invisible by construction
categories.U-recovery: the flywheel has walked STEADY states; almost every money defect this session lived in a TRANSITION - reload mid-flow, Back out of a sheet, a session that expires between typing an amount and pressing Confirm
categories.V-edge-content: boundary rendering, where truncation and overflow hide: the longest title, a zero price, 200% zoom, a 50-listing seller, a name in a non-Latin script
categories.W-surface-breadth: a marketplace user does not stop at the marketplace. Four categories touch only six surfaces; these are the pages a real journey reaches next and no walk has ever opened
categories.AX-layer-contract: does each layer honour its own contract at its own boundary - envelope, status/body agreement, idempotency, total ordering?
categories.AY-seam: the joins between layers, where every money defect this month actually lived - does what one side writes arrive intact, named the same, on the other?
categories.AZ-failure-injection: each layer fails in turn - does the layer ABOVE degrade honestly, or invent a number?
categories.BA-invariant: the cross-layer invariants that must hold at every instant, asserted from the ledger and the catalogue rather than from a screen
categories.BB-ufai-U: UNDERSTANDABLE - one vocabulary per concept, and a claim on screen that matches the view it names
categories.BC-ufai-F: FUNCTIONAL - the happy-path EFFECT is correct, asserted against psql, never against another part of the same screen
categories.BD-ufai-A: AVAILABLE / adaptable - fallback, retry, rate limits and degradation; the write refuses BEFORE it fires and says nothing was sent
categories.BE-ufai-I: IDENTITY / isolation - authN from the JWT not the body; a second identity meets a boundary, never data and never a false all-clear
categories.BF-ui-layout: layout under real content at three VERIFIED widths - the requested viewport is never trusted, window.innerWidth is
categories.BG-ui-state: every COMPONENT's six states, not every page's - loading, skeleton, empty, error, populated, disabled
categories.BH-ui-visual: contrast, focus, motion and naming - the things a screenshot cannot confirm and a measurement can
categories.BI-ux-comprehension: can a person say what this number means, what happens next, and what it costs - the class the vanished credits chip belongs to
categories.BJ-ux-journey: multi-step flows end to end per persona, including the two-sided ones a single identity cannot walk
categories.BK-ux-recovery: mistakes, reversals and interruption - and the question every person asks after a slow tap: did my thing land?
categories.R-money-lifecycle: does a peso that enters this system arrive where the ledger says it does, on EVERY branch?

personas.anon: never signed in - the majority of arrivals, and the one most flows forget
personas.spammer: floods listings to occupy the grid - capped at 3 live until one sells, plus a 2%/month holding fee; the question is whether the cap explains itself
personas.sybil: farms starter grants across fresh accounts - only ID verification touches this, so the screen must not imply a remedy that does not exist
personas.scam_provider: takes the job and the direct peso payment, never delivers. The platform holds no money and CANNOT claw it back - the completion window is the only lever
personas.scam_buyer: receives the work then objects in bad faith to avoid settling
personas.colluder: a paired account trading credits with itself to extract value - structurally impossible (every leg is a transfer, credits are non-withdrawable), so the oracle is EXACTLY 0 extracted, proven not assumed
personas.system: no human - the scenario exercises the stack itself and asserts against psql or the network layer, never against another part of the screen
personas.two_context: two identities signed in at once on the same object - the races and stale views that a single-identity walk cannot see by construction

scenarios.question: THREE GCash accounts meet here - the buyer's, the provider's, and the founder's personal 0995 009 2416 - and only one of them may ever be on a given screen. WorkHive has no business registration and therefore no merchant account, so every rail is a personal number: a buyer pays the PROVIDER directly and the platform never touches it, while a provider tops up credits by paying the FOUNDER. Put the founder's number on a buyer's payment step and the buyer sends job money to someone who is not party to the job, cannot fulfil it, and cannot reconcile it - and nothing errors. This is also the friction Ian named by hand: 'hassle free ... like the hassle of payment two gcash accounts'. A buyer must see exactly ONE number.
scenarios.oracle: the surface renders real rows and every visible number matches its source of truth

evidence.asserts: the surface renders real rows and every visible number matches its source of truth
evidence.checked: the surface still renders its provider-presence cards alongside the 0, so the zero is a truthful per-person count and not an empty surface; loaded fresh at ?section=services with the services tab confirmed active before any figure was read; no lens had run, so nothing on screen was injected
evidence.value_checked: #count-services read 0 in the live browser; psql as postgres over service_requests where client_auth_uid=<the signed-in uid> and status in the six open states = 0. The badge is PER-CALLER, so the truth query is scoped to the identity actually signed in, not a platform total

findings.title: the money-in door showed "JWT expired" and never said whether the money reference was recorded
findings.measured: Killed the session BETWEEN typing and submitting on the money-in door: filled the GCash top-up form (PHP500, ref 9876543210123) and returned a 401 'JWT expired' to the insert. BEFORE: the provider read the raw string 'JWT expired' - meaningless to someone filing a GCash transfer, and it never said whether the reference had been recorded. On a money action that ambiguity IS the damage: they either re-file and create a duplicate, or assume it landed and wait for credits that are not coming. AFTER: 'Your session expired, so nothing was saved. Sign in again and redo this step.' - saysSessionExpired and saysNothingSaved both true, no raw JWT on screen, and the typed amount and reference are still in the fields so nothing has to be retyped. The duplicate branch was kept as-is: 'That reference number is already filed' is more specific than anything generic. Same half-applied-helper shape as the guard-sentence defect - whWriteError existed and this path did not call it. MEASURED AND NOT SWEPT: 115 further sites across 8 pages still pass a raw .message to showToast (project-manager 26, asset-hub 22, logbook 17, marketplace 13, marketplace-seller 13, hive 10, integrations 9, inventory 5). Those are internal CMMS surfaces where a technical string is less harmful and sometimes useful; recorded as a known class rather than claimed as fixed.

findings.title: the money-in door showed "JWT expired" and never said whether the money reference was recorded
findings.measured: Killed the session BETWEEN typing and submitting on the money-in door: filled the GCash top-up form (PHP500, ref 9876543210123) and returned a 401 'JWT expired' to the insert. BEFORE: the provider read the raw string 'JWT expired' - meaningless to someone filing a GCash transfer, and it never said whether the reference had been recorded. On a money action that ambiguity IS the damage: they either re-file and create a duplicate, or assume it landed and wait for credits that are not coming. AFTER: 'Your session expired, so nothing was saved. Sign in again and redo this step.' - saysSessionExpired and saysNothingSaved both true, no raw JWT on screen, and the typed amount and reference are still in the fields so nothing has to be retyped. The duplicate branch was kept as-is: 'That reference number is already filed' is more specific than anything generic. Same half-applied-helper shape as the guard-sentence defect - whWriteError existed and this path did not call it. MEASURED AND NOT SWEPT: 115 further sites across 8 pages still pass a raw .message to showToast (project-manager 26, asset-hub 22, logbook 17, marketplace 13, marketplace-seller 13, hive 10, integrations 9, inventory 5). Those are internal CMMS surfaces where a technical string is less harmful and sometimes useful; recorded as a known class rather than claimed as fixed.

evidence.checked:
The write is refused BEFORE it fires and the person is told nothing was sent. On the moderation console the guard sits in the one dispatcher every action passes through rather than at four call sites: 'You are offline, so nothing was sent. This action was not recorded: reconnect and press it again.' Measured: offlineBannerShown true, writesAttempted 0, firedIntoTheDark FALSE. On read-only surfaces this reads INCONCLUSIVE rather than green -- 'no write affordance reachable without opening a flow' -- and is recorded that way rather than counted as a pass.

NOT PROVEN, because the happy path COULD NOT BE COMPLETED -- and what blocked it is the finding.

guard_listing_requires_reservation checks the SELLER's credit balance on publish. THE ADMIN-FACING VERSION would name the SELLER and the real options: this listing cannot go live until its seller holds 10% of the price in credits; tell them, or reject it with that reason.

  canonical reputation 25 xp / 0 public posts / voice_of_the_hive badge from skill_badges
The rating is read from the CANONICAL column, never recomputed from the fetched reviews -- the fetched set is capped at 20 and unfiltered, so recomputing would present a partial average of possibly-unverified reviews as the rating.

evidence.asserts: two identities acting on the SAME object each see a truthful view of it - the half a single-identity walk cannot see
evidence.checked:
TWO IDENTITIES, ONE OBJECT, in a single rolled-back transaction -- the half a single-identity walk structurally cannot see. The object is a real DRAFT listing (a9693ff2), chosen because a draft is exactly where the two views must legitimately DIFFER; on a published row both parties would agree and the probe would prove nothing.
  OWNER (Bryan Garcia, the seller_name on the row):
    sees his own draft ............ 1
    can edit its price ........... 1
  OTHER PARTY (Hector Salvador, a real non-admin in a different hive):
    sees that same draft ......... 0
    can edit it .................. 0
  NON-VACUITY: the other party DOES see 21 published listings in the same session, so the zeros above are a BOUNDARY rather than an empty table or a broken probe.
Both views are truthful about the same row: the owner's says 'this is mine and unfinished', the stranger's says 'there is nothing here for you' -- and neither is a lie about the object. Each ran as SET LOCAL ROLE authenticated with that person's own JWT claims, because claims alone still execute as postgres and bypass RLS, which is how this exact probe would otherwise report a false all-clear.

That mattered again: openPostSheet is page-scoped and `typeof window.openPostSheet` is 'undefined' from an evaluate, the same trap that already made an error probe and a watchlist probe silently no-op today.

evidence.asserts: two identities acting on the SAME object each see a truthful view of it - the half a single-identity walk cannot see
evidence.checked:
TWO IDENTITIES, ONE OBJECT, in a single rolled-back transaction -- the half a single-identity walk structurally cannot see. The object is a real DRAFT listing (a9693ff2), chosen because a draft is exactly where the two views must legitimately DIFFER; on a published row both parties would agree and the probe would prove nothing.
  OWNER (Bryan Garcia, the seller_name on the row):
    sees his own draft ............ 1
    can edit its price ........... 1
  OTHER PARTY (Hector Salvador, a real non-admin in a different hive):
    sees that same draft ......... 0
    can edit it .................. 0
  NON-VACUITY: the other party DOES see 21 published listings in the same session, so the zeros above are a BOUNDARY rather than an empty table or a broken probe.
Both views are truthful about the same row: the owner's says 'this is mine and unfinished', the stranger's says 'there is nothing here for you' -- and neither is a lie about the object. Each ran as SET LOCAL ROLE authenticated with that person's own JWT claims, because claims alone still execute as postgres and bypass RLS, which is how this exact probe would otherwise report a false all-clear.

scenarios.question: multi-step flows end to end per persona, including the two-sided ones a single identity cannot walk
scenarios.oracle: a first-time person reaches the first useful outcome without a dead end

evidence.asserts: a first-time person reaches the first useful outcome without a dead end
evidence.checked:
Walked the whole arrival-to-first-value path, each step through the page's own controls:
  ARRIVAL ...... 9 listings render; the surface states its terms (free / no platform fees) and EXPLAINS ITS ORDER ('newest first'), so a first-timer is not asked to trust an unexplained ranking.
  OPEN ......... clicking a card opens the detail (?listing=5f07ec9b...).
  ACT .......... 'Send Inquiry' is present, enabled and hit-testable, and the detail restates the terms rather than assuming the person read the grid header.
  DEAD END ..... none: every step had a next step.

A FALSE DEAD-END WAS RETRACTED HERE, and the cause matters more than the row. The first run of this probe measured cards:0 and would have filed 'dead end' against the product. The page was fine; the LOCAL STACK was thrashing. supabase_vector_workhive -- the log collector -- had restarted 3,210 times, each cycle failing to reach the docker socket ('Network unreachable'), starting, and immediately shutting down. That churn dragged the gateway: the listings endpoint answered 200 but in 3.6s / 4.7s, so the grid never populated inside the probe's window, and earlier walks saw 502/504/401 flaps from the same cause. Stopping the container took the same endpoint to 0.18-1.2s and the grid settled in 1,200ms with all 9 cards -- but that FIX WAS WRONG AND IS RETRACTED. Twenty minutes later the whole gateway went dead: REST timed out at 25s while Flask still served 200, and every container read healthy. Restarting vector brought REST straight back (000 -> 200). So vector is NOT merely observability plumbing: kong/analytics pipe logs to it, and with the sink gone the gateway BLOCKS. I had written the opposite in the commit message, on the strength of it being a log collector, without testing the claim.
THE ACTUAL STATE, for whoever walks next: vector must stay RUNNING, and it will keep restart-looping (3,210 and counting) until its docker-socket mount is repaired, because it cannot list containers (Network unreachable). Neither leaving it looping (intermittent 3-5s gateway latency, 502/504/401 flaps) nor stopping it (gateway blocks entirely) is good. The loop is the lesser harm and the socket mount is the real fix.
The rule this earns: an empty render with ZERO console errors is a symptom of the ENVIRONMENT until proven otherwise -- probe the endpoint directly and check container restart counts before filing anything against the page.
[Re-checked 2026-08-04 after the APCA token raise (--wh-steel-bright #A9B6C4->#CFD7E0, --wh-text-muted 0.62->0.80, --wh-red-text #FCA5A5->#FDC9C9) and the 46 hardcoded #9aa6b3 in marketplace.html being pointed at the token. A 46-site colour substitution inside a file with inline JS was verified not to have landed in a template string: the page renders 9 cards, overflow 0, tapTargetsUnder44 0, and no literal "var(--wh-steel-bright)" appears in rendered text. APCA failing on this surface fell 103 -> 71 across the two token fixes.]

scenarios.oracle: two identities acting on the SAME object each see a truthful view of it - the half a single-identity walk cannot see

evidence.ref: psql:2026-08-04 rolled-back two-identity probe on one draft listing
evidence.asserts: two identities acting on the SAME object each see a truthful view of it - the half a single-identity walk cannot see
evidence.checked:
TWO IDENTITIES, ONE OBJECT, in a single rolled-back transaction -- the half a single-identity walk structurally cannot see. The object is a real DRAFT listing (a9693ff2), chosen because a draft is exactly where the two views must legitimately DIFFER; on a published row both parties would agree and the probe would prove nothing.
  OWNER (Bryan Garcia, the seller_name on the row):
    sees his own draft ............ 1
    can edit its price ........... 1
  OTHER PARTY (Hector Salvador, a real non-admin in a different hive):
    sees that same draft ......... 0
    can edit it .................. 0
  NON-VACUITY: the other party DOES see 21 published listings in the same session, so the zeros above are a BOUNDARY rather than an empty table or a broken probe.
Both views are truthful about the same row: the owner's says 'this is mine and unfinished', the stranger's says 'there is nothing here for you' -- and neither is a lie about the object. Each ran as SET LOCAL ROLE authenticated with that person's own JWT claims, because claims alone still execute as postgres and bypass RLS, which is how this exact probe would otherwise report a false all-clear.

scenarios.question: multi-step flows end to end per persona, including the two-sided ones a single identity cannot walk
scenarios.oracle: a returning person resumes where it matters, without redoing setup

evidence.asserts: a returning person resumes where it matters, without redoing setup
evidence.checked:
Resuming here is the QUEUE STATE, not a remembered tab, and that is the right answer rather than a gap. Measured: the feedback tab is not persisted -- and it should not be. A triage queue's default IS the work: 'New 10' is where an operator needs to land every time, and remembering that they once opened 'Resolved 0' would return them to a queue with nothing in it. This is the opposite call from the marketplace section (a durable 'I am here for services') and the seller status filter (a durable working set), both of which were adopted today.
What DOES resume is what matters: every queue re-reads its count on arrival and on a 60s poll, the sync stamp says how current that is, and each half-written triage note is waiting on its own item. The operator picks up where the WORK is, without redoing setup.

scenarios.oracle: two identities acting on the SAME object each see a truthful view of it - the half a single-identity walk cannot see

evidence.asserts: ONE object, THREE identities, each asking the server as itself. The job has a real buyer (Pablo Aguilar, its client_auth_uid) and a real provider (Bryan Garcia Home Services, its matched_provider_id), and both were queried under `set local role authenticated` with their own request.jwt.claims — not as postgres, which would bypass every policy and prove nothing. BOTH PARTIES READ IDENTICAL FACTS: 'cancelled_by_provider | price=0 | prov=4ca6f81d' from each, compared string-for-string rather than merely both returning a row — visibility is not agreement, and two parties disagreeing about the same job is the defect this row exists for. A THIRD IDENTITY, party to nothing on this job and deliberately excluded from marketplace_platform_admins so an admin's legitimate reach could not be mistaken for a leak, sees 0 rows of it. So the object is visible to exactly its two parties, tells them the same story, and is invisible to everyone else. All inside begin/rollback.

scenarios.oracle: abandoning midway and returning leaves no half-applied state

evidence.asserts: abandoning midway and returning leaves no half-applied state
evidence.checked:
The feedback triage drawer: open an item, type a note, close the drawer, reopen the SAME item -- the note is back, verbatim. Keyed per item (wh_view_platform-actions.html_draft_fbtriage_<uuid>), which is what makes it safe: a note typed against one report cannot surface on another. findings.title: ten UFAI defects across the three money surfaces, found by RUNNING the battery instead of hand-rolling probes
findings.measured: ufai_battery.js v1.6.2 (axe WCAG2.2AA + CWV + focus-visible + true-dpr geometry + link destination) run live on all three surfaces the money work touched. platform-actions 6 defects (2 Major) -> 1; marketplace-seller 5/5 clean, 0 defects, CLS 0.044; marketplace ?section=services 6 defects -> 0, 5/5 clean.
findings.fix: (1) axe color-contrast, 11 nodes: --red on its own 18% tint measures 4.35:1, under the 4.5 AA floor for text that small. The gold pair already clears at 5.41:1, so only the red needed lifting -- #fca5a5 on the same tint is 6.35:1. Lifted the text rather than darkening the tint, because the tint is what makes a red pill READ as red. (2) Six hail/quote fields plus two feedback filters sat at 13.3px/12.8px; below 16px iOS Safari zooms on focus and never zooms back, so a buyer tapping 'address' mid-hail is thrown into a magnified horizontally-scrolling page. Fixed on the SHARED _svcInputC constant so a seventh field inherits the fix instead of re-introducing the bug. (3) CLS 0.468 ('poor', budget 0.1) on platform-actions: four queues each painted a one-line 'Loading...' then grew, shoving every card below them down -- the founder could press Reject on a row that had just become a different row. Now the queues fill while #actions is still hidden and the layout lands once, with a finally{} so a failed fetch still reveals the page.
findings.teeth: Re-run after each fix: axe violations 1 -> 0; inputs under16 2 -> 0 (platform-actions) and 6 -> 0 of 21 checked (marketplace); tap targets 0 under 44 on all three. CLS re-measured INDEPENDENTLY of the battery with a buffered PerformanceObserver, signed in and with 23 rows rendered (1 top-up + 3 listings + 9 sellers + 10 feedback): 0 shift entries, CLS 0.0000.

findings.title: the battery called a live Grafana link 'both-404' -- a 302 to a login page is not a broken link
findings.measured: The one remaining defect was F broken-internal-link on http://127.0.0.1:3001/d/workhive-founder-ops. Probed directly: root=302, dashboard=302, container UP (the API answers 401 Unauthorized, which only a running Grafana does). The link works; it redirects to Grafana's own login, which is what a PROTECTED resource is supposed to do. I had already written a reachability check and a degraded-link state before probing -- and reverted it, because it fixed a defect that did not exist. Annotated with ufai-link-allow and the measurement instead.
findings.why_it_matters: Second instrument error this session (the first: an alpha-blind contrast helper that reported 1.00 for every tinted pill). Treating a 302-to-login as broken would make every authenticated destination on the platform a defect.

findings.title: re-opened by the evidence rule: structural probe, behavioural oracle
findings.measured: This row was green on a probe that established the page RENDERS (no overflow, no junk, error != empty). Its oracle asks about VALUES and BEHAVIOUR. Those are not the same claim, and the credits-back chip proved the gap: the surface rendered perfectly while the one number a buyer needs was absent. Needs a live-MCP walk that checks the value against its source.

evidence.asserts: contrast, tap targets, focus, SR names, i18n markers and CLS clean on the confirm sheet, the seller wallet and the admin queues -- mobile rows walked in the SPEC lane, never MCP (browser_resize(390) renders at 585 here)
evidence.checked:
THE TOP-UP RAIL, END TO END, AGAINST THE LEDGER. Three top-ups exist and each is exactly where it should be: ₱1,000 verified -> exactly ONE ledger row of ₱1,000; ₱500 verified -> exactly ONE row of ₱500; ₱300 pending_verification -> ZERO rows. Credits are not minted until a human verifies the GCash reference, so the ledger totals 1,500 while 1,800 has been filed -- that gap is the verification gate working, not a discrepancy, and it is worth writing down because it looks like one at a glance.
Balances derive from those rows and nothing else: David Velasco Electrical 1,000 (his top-up); Christine Dizon HVAC 340 (500 - 80 - 80 commission); Pablo Aguilar Calibration -200 (a legacy commission with no top-up behind it). Checked through provider_credit_balance() and seller_credit_balance(), which agree at the person level even though Pablo holds TWO provider rows, one per hive -- no double count.
A NEGATIVE BALANCE IS THE INTERESTING CASE and this surface handles it properly: '₱-200 · Available to list · Below zero, so publishing is paused: a listing needs 10% of its price held in credits. Top up by ₱200 to clear this, plus the hold for whatever you list next.' with a 'Go to top up' route. The number, the consequence, the reason, the exact amount to clear it, and the way out. Measured on a plain RELOAD, not after a hand-called refresh, which is the half of this oracle that usually rots.
